## Decision: DON'T SHIP

## Primary result
- **conversion** (primary, higher is better): treatment vs control **+11.6% (95% CI +4.18% to +19%), p = 0.0012; absolute +0.01147 (0.09908 -> 0.1105); better** [r3]
- One treatment arm, so no primary multiple-testing adjustment was needed [r1].

## Guardrails
- **bounce** (guardrail, higher is worse, margin 5%): treatment vs control **+3.45% (95% CI -0.124% to +7.03%), p = 0.054; absolute +0.01019 (0.295 -> 0.3052); inconclusive; guardrail FAILED (worst case +7.03% vs margin 5%)** [r4]
- The guardrail did not pass, so the ship condition is not met even though the primary metric improved.

## Validity checks (SRM, peeking, novelty)
- **SRM**: passed. Observed split control 49.79% / treatment 50.21%; chi2 = 0.5125, p = 0.47 [r2].
- **Peeking**: no planned interim looks [r1], so no sequential test was run.
- **Novelty**: no daily data available (`has_daily = false`) [r1], so daily effects could not be checked.
- **CUPED**: no pre-period conversion covariate was available (covariates are pre_revenue and pre_sessions) [r1], so no CUPED adjustment was applied.

## Caveats
- The decision is driven entirely by the guardrail failure: the bounce CI's worst case (+7.03%) exceeds the pre-registered 5% margin [r4]. The primary conversion win cannot override this under the pre-registered decision rule.
- Observed n reached the planned 30,000 [r1]; the decision is not an underpowered-extension case.

## Exploratory findings
- None run.
